summary.intent: Improve memory quality in the checkpoint repo's memory loop by adding a hard evidence gate that rejects one-off or unverifiable memories, replacing the existing prompt-instruction-only approach.
summary.outcome: Implemented a two-layer evidence gate (provenance + session validation) in generator.go, replacing passesReviewDerivedGate with a generalized passesEvidenceGate. All tests pass and CI is green. Also fixed a JSON parse error caused by LLM returning trailing text after the JSON object.

repo: AffectedSessions in PatternAnalysis uses CheckpointID, but the generation prompt was exposing SessionID — these must be aligned to the same identifier type for the evidence gate to work.
passesReviewDrivedGate at generator.go:360 was the only kind-specific evidence enforcement; all other memory kinds (repo_rule, workflow_rule, agent_instruction) had no multi-session requirement.
repo_learning and workflow_learning in PatternAnalysis have no Count or AffectedSessions fields, making them ineligible for the evidence gate — they must be marked context-only in the prompt.
Personal-scope records auto-activate without a TUI promotion step (memoryloop.go:623), so UI-only quality controls are insufficient.

llmcli.ExtractJSONFromMarkdown at llmcli.go:122 handles markdown-fenced JSON but not trailing plain text after a bare JSON object — raw unmarshal fails with 'invalid character n after top-level value'.
logicalRuleSimilarity is defined in memoryloop.go and used there too, not only in the review gate helpers — must not be removed when removing passesReviewDerivedGate.
GenerationStats is consumed in both memoryloop.go (RefreshHistory) and memory_loop_cmd.go (display) — new fields must be propagated to both.

code.finding: Prompt instruction 'Avoid duplicates and avoid one-off incidents without repeated evidence' is a suggestion to the LLM, not a hard code gate.
Post-filter catches low confidence and low strength, but a one-off memory with confidence:high and strength:4 passes through.
SourceSessionIDs was captured but never validated for length — a record backed by 1 session was treated identically to one backed by 5.
passesReviewDerivedGate enforced count>=2 || strong only for review-derived rules, not for other kinds. Replaced by generalized passesEvidenceGate.
Personal-scope records become active immediately under auto-activation policy, bypassing TUI review entirely.

workflow: When an LLM fills structured fields (like source_session_ids), those fields can be hallucinated — gate on upstream analyzer aggregations (RecurringSignal.Count, AffectedSessions) rather than trusting LLM-populated fields alone.
Iterative design review with Codex caught: (1) missing provenance link making cross-reference fuzzy, (2) allow-on-no-match fallback nullifying the gate, (3) auto-activation bypassing TUI controls.
Write analysis doc to shared file for async review by other agents before implementing.
Run mise lint after implementation to confirm no new lint issues introduced in changed files.

friction: Identifier mismatch between AffectedSessions (CheckpointID) and prompt sessions (SessionID) required a prerequisite fix before the evidence gate could be deterministic.

LLM returned trailing natural language text after JSON object despite 'Return ONLY JSON' instruction, causing json.Unmarshal to fail with 'invalid character n after top-level value' — required adding extractJSONObject helper.
Twelve existing tests had to be updated to include SourceSignal provenance fields plus matching analysis signals, since the new gate rejects records without valid provenance.

passesReviewDerivedGate and its helpers (bestMatchingReviewDerivedRule, generatedMatchesReviewEvidence) had to be carefully decomposed — the literal review evidence rejection needed to be preserved as a standalone isLiteralReviewEvidence check.
open_items: improve/generator.go and facets/facets.go may have the same LLM trailing-text JSON parse issue — not fixed in this session.
Existing low-quality memories already in memory-loop.json are not affected by the new gate — no backfill or re-evaluation pass was implemented.
Option 4 (show evidence count in TUI before promotion) is still useful for transparency alongside the evidence gate but was not implemented.
repo_learning and workflow_learning could be given Count/AffectedSessions fields upstream in the analyzer to make them eligible for the evidence gate in the future.

The substring-fallback in findRecurringSignal/findSkillSignal/findReviewRuleSignal may produce false positives if LLM paraphrases keys — exact match behavior and false-negative rate should be monitored.
